title: Incremental shadow waveform and cost-anchoring pipeline
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: We need a safe, low-cost shadowing/mirroring pipeline to validate new model variants in production without exposing customer-facing traffic or exceeding tenant budgets. Existing shadowing solutions either duplicate full payloads (expensive) or sample naively (risking bias and missed regressions).

Goal: Build an "incremental shadow waveform" pipeline that duplicates only a calibrated fraction of traffic in waves, anchors cost using per-tenant credit fences and a cost-anchoring controller, and isolates shadow executions so they cannot affect production state. The pipeline should support gradual expansion, deterministic sampling for reproducible analytics, automatic rollback triggers based on quality regressions or cost drift, and observability hooks for per-route and per-tenant shadow metrics.

Scope: Implement a gateway-side traffic demultiplexer that produces shadow waves (time-boxed windows of increasing sampling rate), a credit-anchoring controller that prevents tenants from exceeding allocated shadow credits, a sandboxed execution path (no side-effects, strict RBAC), and a rollout policy that can auto-halt/rollback on objective regressions (latency/LLM-quality) or if shadow spend approaches a safety threshold.

Non-goals: This ticket does not implement UI in Console; it focuses on runtime, controller logic, and APIs for signals. UI/Console wiring will be a follow-up ticket.
progress_updates: 2026-02-20 - Initial scoping and design spike. Identified three failure modes: uncontrolled spend, biased sample leading to false negatives, and side-effect leakage. Decided on wave-based ramp plus deterministic hashing for reproducibility.

2026-02-27 - PoC: gateway demux implemented in a feature branch (github.com/redwood-inference/ml-infra/pulls/2143). PoC supports fixed-wave progression and deterministic tenant hashing. KV-cache warmup simulated for short inputs.

2026-03-03 - Design review with SRE and PM. Agreed on per-tenant soft-credit and hard-credit fences, and on a two-tier circuit-breaker: controller-level global guard and tenant-level hard stop. SRE requested explicit telemetry for shadow CPU/GPU seconds per tenant.

2026-03-08 - Integration test: sandboxed path enforced via request-level RBAC token and network namespace. Verified no outbound side-effects in 1000-sample synthetic run. Found a bug where batched KV cache entries were incorrectly reused across shadow context — hotfix landed in PR #2190.

2026-03-12 - Started canary of small tenant cohort (10 tenants, <1% of traffic). Monitoring dashboard: latency delta within SLA, cost drift 0.6% of predicted budget. One alert for model-quality regression on a specific prompt set — triggered rollback hook for that model variant while leaving other waves running.
acceptance_criteria: Gateway demultiplexer can emit shadow waves with configurable schedule and deterministic sampling by tenant and route.
Per-tenant soft and hard credit fences are enforced; when soft threshold crossed send telemetry and reduce sampling; when hard threshold crossed stop shadowing for that tenant.
Sandboxed execution path prevents side-effects: no outbound network egress from shadow tasks, no writes to production databases, and logs tagged for shadow-only retention policy.
Controller exposes metrics: shadow-tokenized-tokens, shadow-GPU-seconds, shadow-failure-rate, sample-delta-by-route; dashboards and alerts wired to SRE runbook.
Auto-rollback triggers for quality regression (by eval set delta) and sustained latency/timeout increases; rollback action is recorded and model variant pinned back to previous stable for routing.
End-to-end smoke tests and a staged canary (10 tenants -> 50 tenants -> 200 tenants) complete without exceeding a cost budget of 2% of normal inference spend for the canary cohort.
Design doc and API spec reviewed and approved by PM, SRE, and Security.
